answer: The atlas multiplier is published, charged in lotus, and timber lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 4966 identities would post 4083 proofs and burn roughly 27 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
